data.title: Route Overview
paragraphs: This route begins on the Malabar coast but quickly climbs into Wayanad’s plateau, where forest edges, farms, and indigenous histories require slower, locally guided exploration. From there it descends toward Nilambur’s teak country and the cultural landscape of the Nila.

Rather than chasing a long list of sights, the journey is built around three connected landscapes: upland forest, foothill timber country, and river plain. Each is given enough time for walking, conversation, food, and small-scale cultural encounters.

data.title: Journey Standards & Inclusions
items: Forest-edge lodges and rural stays selected for quiet settings and responsible access.
Private transfers timed to avoid rushed same-day sightseeing after long drives.
Naturalists and craft specialists brought in for focused interpretation.
Community visits arranged only through appropriate local partners.

data.title: Suggested Packing & Preparation
items: Light layers for variable plateau temperatures.
Closed shoes suitable for forest-edge and farm walking.
Rain protection for Wayanad outside the driest months.
Modest casual clothing for village and home visits.
A small daypack and reusable bottle for walking days.

data.quote: Northern Kerala is at its best when the road leaves the coast, climbs through forest, and returns to the plains carrying stories with it.

data.title: FOREST ACCESS NOTE
data.text: Protected-area access, trail permissions, and community visits can change with weather and local regulations. The route uses flexible alternatives rather than forcing a fixed wildlife schedule.

data.title: From Canopy to River Plain
paragraphs: Wayanad, Nilambur, and the Nila are rarely experienced as one connected journey, yet the transition between them is precisely what gives this route its character.
The memories are quieter: wet earth after rain, pepper vines on a farm, a loom in motion, teak shadows, and the wide river opening toward Palakkad.

items.question: Can this route be tailored to our preferred dates and pace?
paragraphs: Yes. Every Signature itinerary is a design framework, and we adjust nights, experiences, transport, and daily intensity around your interests and travel dates.

items.question: Is this a wildlife safari itinerary?
paragraphs: No. Nature is central, but the emphasis is on landscape, ecology, farms, and guided walking rather than vehicle safaris.

items.question: Can we add more time in Wayanad?
paragraphs: Yes. Wayanad is the easiest section to extend for additional nature, wellness, or farm-based experiences.

items.question: Which airport works best?
paragraphs: Calicut is ideal for arrival; departure can be planned through Coimbatore, Calicut, or Kochi depending on the final route.

items.question: What is included when the final journey is quoted?
paragraphs: The final proposal clearly separates accommodation, private transport, guiding, arranged experiences, and any route-specific permits or specialist access.
items.listTitle: The exact inclusion list is confirmed before payment:
listItems: Chosen accommodation category and meal plan.
Confirmed guiding, hosted encounters, and ticketed experiences.
Any permits or special-access costs included in the final design.

items.question: How are reservations confirmed and scheduled?
paragraphs: Once the bespoke route, accommodation selection, and current supplier availability are approved, a 30% confirmation deposit secures the agreed services. The remaining balance is due 45 days before arrival unless the final proposal states otherwise.

items.question: What is the policy for date changes or cancellations?
paragraphs: We work directly with our partners to move dates whenever possible. Any non-refundable permits, transport tickets, or supplier penalties are passed through transparently.
listItems: 60+ days before arrival: deposit refund less confirmed non-refundable costs.
30–59 days before arrival: 50% refund or travel credit where supplier terms allow.
Less than 30 days before arrival: cancellation follows the confirmed supplier terms in your final proposal.
